notes: Building and Industrial News, vol. 11 part 1 (Internet Archive buildingindustri11111cont), the 25 weekly issues from 7 January to 27 June 1911: Saturdays through 8 April, Tuesdays from 18 April (no issue is dated between 8 and 18 April, and the cover numbers run 1 to 25 without a gap). Same method as the later volumes of this source: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll year fits, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before the work. The issues were dated from their covers. The item numbers restart at 1 in the second January issue, and in March and April many are printed with a full stop inside the bracket ('(773.)'), which extract.py now accepts. The street is printed first, as in vol. 11 pt. 2 (place.py with BEN_STREET_FIRST=1), and the OCR of this volume reads N as X and W as AV or \V ('Sutter X 50 E Steiner', 'Chenery Xo. 894'); the heading reader now turns these back, which raised the picked rows from 113 to 179. Nine item numbers the OCR misread were corrected from the page image. Every published row was read against the page image, location first. Many entries in this volume run past the foot of a column, so the crop shows only the head of the entry; the rest was then read from the OCR lines that follow, a name taken where the line is clean and a cost only where the instalments add up to the printed total, which leaves a number of contracts and permits without a cost. Owners who are private individuals are never recorded, nor is a contractor or architect who is the owner, shares the owner's surname, or is listed at the owner's premises; sureties are cut. Held back at the image (47 of 179): minor work such as signs, shop fittings and small repairs (18), contracts the page already carries in full from the San Francisco Call (7), storey counts that contradict the roll (6), unit counts that contradict the roll, among them single dwellings on parcels the roll gives two units (6), and small alterations and plain single houses on parcels with no page (10, held for a page). 29 rows on pages that already carry a Call entry of the same weeks (the 1906-1913 newspaper recovery) were trimmed to what this paper adds (the architect, the contractor, the kind of building or the price). Where the price differs from the Call entry the page image read here is given and the Call entry left alone (1766 Union Street: $8,500 here, four instalments of $2,125, against $8,300; 1920 Taylor Street: $5,720 here, instalments of $953, $953, $954 and $2,860, against $3,720). An alteration or a trade contract does not set a building's builder. The loft building at Ninth and Tehama (item 615) has a parcel with no EAS row and stays unresolved. At Central Avenue and Grove the permit of March 1911 and a second permit of August 1913 (vol. 13 pt. 2, held until now, its cost corrected from $75,000 in the OCR to $7,000 on the image) are both on the page; the roll dates the building 1913, so the 1911 permit may not be the building that stands. A held fact of the Bay Area Reporter (a 1980 opening at 2360 Van Ness Avenue) was taken up on a page seeded here.

coverage.remaining: Nothing is left to read: all eight half-year volumes on the Internet Archive are done. In this volume: 123 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; they still need the image check), and 10 more were held for a page at the image. 827 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today. The rest have a nearest parcel that was not accepted.
